did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 8 states that Solomon’s building projects lasted twenty years, during which he built the Temple of the LORD and his own palace.
Did you know? The cities Hiram gave to Solomon did not remain as they were; Solomon rebuilt them and settled Israelites in them.
Did you know? Solomon went to war against Hamath-zobah, showing that the chapter describes a military aspect of his reign alongside his building projects.
Did you know? Among Solomon’s building projects were Tadmor in the wilderness and the store cities he built in Hamath—cities apparently intended for storage and supplies.
Did you know? Solomon fortified Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, which the text describes as fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars.

Did you know? In addition to the store cities, Solomon built chariot cities and cities for horsemen, as well as everything else he wished to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land under his rule.
Did you know? The Canaanite peoples who remained in the land—including the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—are described as people who were not Israelites.
Did you know? According to the chapter, the Israelites were not employed as slaves in the building work; they served as soldiers, commanders, chariot officers, and horsemen.
Did you know? Solomon moved Pharaoh’s daughter from the City of David to the house he had built for her because he said the City of David was holy, since the Ark of the LORD had entered it.
Did you know? Hiram sent Solomon ships and sailors skilled in seafaring, and they sailed with Solomon’s men to Ophir and brought the king 450 talents of gold.
